title: [Chapitre] III. Réseaux via découpages : notes manuscrites (08/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 35-37). Grothendieck is axiomatizing a 'topological' structure M on a partial lattice of 'admissible' pieces. In the intended model, M = Mod(L) is built from strata of a dissection ('découpage') attached to a configuration L. M has a 0, a 1, a complement, and meet and join. These operations are only well behaved on pairs or triples that are 'modulaires' (mutually compatible: their Boolean combinations stay in M and distributivity holds). M also carries a closure operator X -> X-bar, with the notions 'fermé' and 'ouvert' (closed and open).

Induced structure. For A in M, M_A is the induced structure on A: the X ⊂ A, X in M, modular with A, with relative complement C_A. Page 35 checks that M_A again satisfies the axioms (items 1-6).

Top of p.36 finishes item 6. The closed sets of M_A are Z = Y ∧ A with Y closed in M, {Y,A} modular. Those containing X correspond to Y ⊇ X, i.e. Y ⊇ X-bar. The smallest is Y = X-bar, so
  closure^{M_A}(X) = closure^M(X) ∧ A.

Next he checks that relative closure commutes with joins of modular pairs X, Y in M_A:
  cl^{M_A}(X ∨ Y) = cl^M(X ∨ Y) ∧ A = (X-bar ∨ Y-bar) ∧ A = (X-bar ∧ A) ∨ (Y-bar ∧ A) = cl^A(X) ∨ cl^A(Y).
This is the Kuratowski additivity axiom for the induced structure.

Item 7 checks the compatibility needed above. If X, Y lie in M_A with {X,Y} modular, then {X,Y,A} is modular, hence {X-bar,Y,A} is modular, hence {X-bar ∧ A, Y} is modular. 'OK'.

Connected components. M is connected if every clopen X is 0 or 1. NB: one expects a clopen X to be modular with every Y. If so, the clopen elements form a Boolean algebra. When this Boolean algebra is finite (next page), the connected components are the minimal nonzero clopen elements, assuming 0 ≠ 1.

The next page tests this on M = Mod(L) with A = X_Φ = ∪ T_i, a union of strata of a flag. It claims the components of A are the T_i, and starts the proof: A = ∨ T_i, the T_i pairwise disjoint, each T_i clopen in A and connected.

Purpose: an abstract, lattice-theoretic 'tame topology' framework in which stratified pieces of a dissection (réseaux via découpages) behave like subspaces with closure and connected components, without point-set topology.
errors: The distributivity step (X-bar ∨ Y-bar) ∧ A = (X-bar ∧ A) ∨ (Y-bar ∧ A) is valid only if the triple {X-bar, Y-bar, A} is modular/compatible. Item 7 only shows {X-bar, Y, A}; the symmetric step for Y-bar is implicit. It follows by applying the same argument again, but this is not written.
The equality cl^M(X ∨ Y) = X-bar ∨ Y-bar for modular pairs is used as an axiom of M without being restated.

The claim that clopen elements are modular with every Y is only 'expected' ('on s'attend'), not proved. So the Boolean algebra of clopens, and hence the definition of components, is conditional on this page.

ideas.what: Subspace closure equals ambient closure intersected with the subspace, in an abstract partial lattice with closure
ideas.modern_name: Relative closure in a subspace; closure algebras (McKinsey–Tarski) relativized

ideas.what: Closure operator on a lattice where joins/meets/complements are only controlled on 'modular' (compatible) families, with induced structures M_A
ideas.modern_name: Partial Boolean algebra / compatibility structure with a closure operator; o-minimal-style 'tame' family of definable sets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Partial Boolean algebras: Kochen–Specker (1967); tame topology / o-minimality: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn (1980s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) §5-6 only sketches 'topologie modérée' as a programme; this specific formalism is not there

ideas.what: Connectedness as the absence of nontrivial clopen elements; components as atoms of the (finite) Boolean algebra of clopens
ideas.modern_name: Connected components via Boolean algebra of clopens (Stone-type viewpoint)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (Stone 1936 for the Boolean algebra of clopens)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches an axiomatic, point-free 'tame topology' on a partial lattice of strata, with compatibility ('modular') conditions, closure, induced structures and connected components. It is meant for dissections ('découpages') of configurations. The theory (proof that clopens are universally compatible, components of strata unions) is left in progress. It is a concrete instance of the 'topologie modérée' programme of the Esquisse, distinct from o-minimality.
missed.quote: On dit que M est connexe si ∀X∈M, X fermé et X ouvert ⟹ X=∅ ou X=1 ... On s'attend qu'il soit mod. avec ∀Y
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a lattice-theoretic axiomatization of stratified tame spaces. It could be compared with o-minimal structures, constructible topologies and closure algebras on partial Boolean algebras. Its details are mostly routine on this page.

deep.surprise_reason: The page carries out routine verifications: relative closure, additivity, compatibility and the definition of connectedness. They sit inside an unusual unpublished axiomatic framework for 'tame' stratified topology. The framework itself is mildly interesting, but nothing on this page is a striking result.
transcription_corrections: What the transcription reads as 'médiant' is most likely 'modulaire'/'mod.' (cursive abbreviation), consistent with the previous page's '{X,Y} mod'.
'On s'attend qu'il soit médiateur Y' should read roughly 'On s'attend qu'il soit mod. avec ∀Y' (modular with every Y).
In the first displayed join the left side was first written 'XXY' with the middle X corrected; it means X∨Y.
'M_A^#' in item 7 is uncertain; it may be M_A with a superscript A or a correction mark, i.e. simply M_A.
The last two lines are largely illegible. They concern the clopen X forming a Boolean algebra ('une algèbre de Boole'), which continues on the next page with 'de Boole en question est finie'.
